title: Order total drifts because prices are summed as binary floats
description: checkout/total.py sums line-item prices with float arithmetic. Support reports customer totals that are off by one cent.
acceptance_criteria: The result must be exact for two-decimal currency values.
Existing callers of `total` must keep working.
No third-party dependencies may be added.
constraints: Keep the public signature of `total` unchanged.

files.content:
"""Order total calculation."""


def total(items: list[dict]) -> float:
    """Sum the price of every item."""
    result = 0.0
    for item in items:
        result = result + float(item["price"])
    return result

expected_findings.summary: Summing currency in binary float accumulates representation error; 0.1 + 0.2 != 0.3.

title: User search interpolates the query term into SQL
description: search.py builds a LIKE query with an f-string. The term comes from a query parameter on a public search page.
acceptance_criteria: The term must never be able to change the shape of the statement.

expected_findings.summary: The term is interpolated into the statement, so it can close the literal and inject arbitrary SQL.
execute() with a single argument cannot be parameterised, so the injection has no parameter binding protecting it.

title: Listing endpoint loads every row into memory
description: The audit log page fetches all events and filters in Python. It has been fine at 10k rows and is now timing out at 4M.
acceptance_criteria: The endpoint must return in constant memory regardless of table size.

files.content:
from app.db import get_conn


def all_events(conn) -> list[dict]:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT * FROM audit_events ORDER BY created_at")
        return [row for row in cur.fetchall() if row["actor"]]

expected_findings.token: cur.execute("SELECT * FROM audit_events ORDER BY created_at")
expected_findings.summary: The whole table is read before filtering, so memory grows with the table and the filter is wasted work.
SELECT * pulls every column including large payloads the caller discards.

title: Job queue polls a filtered column that is not indexed
description: The worker polls for jobs that are ready. Latency grew linearly with queue depth and EXPLAIN shows a sequential scan.
acceptance_criteria: Polling must not degrade as the queue grows.

expected_findings.summary: The poll filters on status and orders by run_after with no supporting index, so it is a sequential scan per poll.

title: Auth token is accepted without checking its expiry
description: A logout on one device does not end the session elsewhere, and old tokens still work weeks later.
acceptance_criteria: An expired token must be rejected.

expected_findings.summary: decode() verifies the signature but does not enforce exp, so an expired token is accepted indefinitely.

title: Import crashes on non-ASCII customer names
description: The nightly import fails with UnicodeDecodeError on any file containing an accented name.
acceptance_criteria: UTF-8 input must import without error and round-trip names exactly.

expected_findings.summary: open() uses the platform default encoding, so a UTF-8 file is decoded as ASCII and raises on any non-ASCII byte.

title: Client retries in a tight loop and takes the API down
description: During a partner outage the client retried 200 times a second, which is what turned a degradation into an outage.
acceptance_criteria: Retries must be bounded and spaced.

expected_findings.summary: The retry loop has no delay, so a failing dependency receives 200 requests a second from every client at once.
Every transport error is swallowed identically, so a 4xx (permanent) is retried the same 200 times as a timeout.

title: Feature flag never fires because None is compared with is
description: The new pricing rollout did not activate for anyone, and the flag reads as enabled in the config file.
acceptance_criteria: The flag must take effect for users in the rollout cohort.

expected_findings.summary: `is` compares identity, so a string built or loaded separately never matches COHORT and the flag is permanently False.

title: Handler accumulates state across requests because the default is mutable
description: The per-tenant bucket list is shared between every request; one noisy tenant fills everyone else's allowance.
acceptance_criteria: Each caller must get its own accumulator.

expected_findings.summary: A mutable default argument is evaluated once and shared by every call, so state leaks across requests and across tenants.

title: Download endpoint serves arbitrary files
description: A tester reported that passing ../../etc/passwd to the download route returns the file.
acceptance_criteria: A request may not escape the export directory.

expected_findings.summary: os.path.join discards the root when name is absolute or contains .., so the caller controls the path entirely.

title: Cleanup failure is swallowed, leaking connections
description: Connection pool usage grows steadily and the service eventually refuses new work, with no error anywhere in the logs.
acceptance_criteria: A cleanup failure must be visible.

expected_findings.summary: A blanket except with pass discards the reason the connection could not be returned, so the pool leaks with no diagnostic.
checkin is inside the try, so a rollback failure means the connection is never returned to the pool at all.

title: Test suite passes against code it does not exercise
description: A regression in the parser was merged and CI stayed green.
acceptance_criteria: The test must fail when the parser is wrong.

expected_findings.summary: The assertion only checks that something came back; it never compares against the expected date, so any non-None value passes.

title: Debug logging is evaluated even when disabled
description: A hot loop renders a multi-kilobyte payload per iteration even in production, where the log level filters it out.
acceptance_criteria: Disabled logging must cost nothing.

files.content:
import logging

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def handle(event: dict) -> None:
    log.debug(f"event received: {event}")
    process(event)

expected_findings.summary: The f-string is evaluated before log.debug decides to discard it, so the formatting cost is paid on every iteration.

title: Scheduled job runs at the wrong time after a DST change
description: The nightly job started an hour early after the clocks changed, then an hour late six months later.
acceptance_criteria: The schedule must be expressed in an absolute timezone.

expected_findings.summary: now() returns local time on whatever host it runs on, so the 03:00 target shifts with the host's timezone and DST.

title: Two workers stampede the same cache key
description: At peak, upstream receives a burst of identical requests for one hot key, tripping their rate limit.
acceptance_criteria: One hot key must produce one upstream request.

expected_findings.summary: The check and the fill are not atomic, so N concurrent readers all miss and all call fetch_upstream for the same key.

title: Pagination loop never terminates on a truncated response
description: A partner API returned a repeated page once and the importer looped until it was killed.
acceptance_criteria: The loop must terminate on a repeated or empty page.

expected_findings.summary: The loop has no exit and no emptiness check, so a repeated or empty page appends forever.
Nothing detects a page identical to the previous one, which is exactly how the loop becomes infinite.

title: API key committed to the repository
description: A security scanner flagged a credential in the settings module; it has been in git history for four months.
acceptance_criteria: No credential may live in the source tree.

files.content:
DEBUG = False

PAYMENTS_API_KEY = "EXAMPLE_PAYMENTS_TOKEN_DO_NOT_USE"
DATABASE_URL = "postgres://checkout:hunter2@db.internal:5432/checkout"

expected_findings.summary: A live API secret is committed in plaintext; it must be revoked and moved to the environment or a secret manager.
A database URL with an inline password is committed, so the credential is in the repository and in every clone.

title: Deleting a user takes the API down
description: Account deletion degraded every request for minutes. The foreign key on orders.user_id has no index.
acceptance_criteria: Deletion must be bounded work.

files.content:
def delete(conn, user_id: str) -> None:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("DELETE FROM orders WHERE user_id = %s", (user_id,))
        cur.execute("DELETE FROM users WHERE id = %s", (user_id,))

expected_findings.summary: The predicate is an unindexed foreign key, so the delete is a full scan of orders and holds locks for its duration.

title: Optional field is used without being checked
description: A 500 with AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'email' reaches the logs whenever a user has no profile.
acceptance_criteria: A user without a profile must render, not raise.

expected_findings.summary: profile is optional in the model, so an active user with no profile raises AttributeError instead of falling back.

title: Export is written to a predictable temporary file
description: Two exports on one host occasionally clobber each other, and an unprivileged local user can read the contents in between.
acceptance_criteria: The file must be created atomically with exclusive access.

files.content:
import csv


def write(rows: list[dict], dest: str) -> None:
    with open(dest + "/export.csv", "w", newline="") as handle:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(handle, fieldnames=["id", "total"])
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerows(rows)

expected_findings.summary: A fixed, predictable path opened with mode 'w' is world-readable in between and two concurrent exports overwrite each other.
